newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria plans to re-award oil lifting contracts.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria plans to re-award oil lifting contracts.

text.p: Nigeria plans to soon re-award crude oil lifting contracts terminated by the military government early last year, oil industry executives said on Tuesday.
They said this would reduce the amount of Nigerian crude oil available on the spot market and allow much of the nation's oil to be sold on term contracts.
"Negotiations are on and many of the former term buyers are likely to have the new contracts," said one oil source.

The Lagos-based independent newspaper THISDAY reported on Tuesday that among the oil firms that currently have spot lifting contracts were Arcadia, Vitol, Addax and Glencore, who are known players in the Nigerian oil scene.
Nigeria cancelled term contracts last year and reverted to spot sales when world oil prices were robust.
Spot sales saw much of Nigerian crude oil going to the Far East instead of traditional markets in the West.
Industry sources said indigenous oil firms such as Consolidated and Amni International were likely to feature among the beneficiaries of the new term contracts.

Nigeria currently pumps around 2.1 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil and has about one million bpd available for lifting after subtracting the 250,000 bpd for domestic refining and what is due to its foreign joint venture partners.
